verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 9% to $8.6B and net income jumped 17% to $4.9B, as cross-border spending stayed strong and the prior year's $341M litigation provision did not repeat.

kpis.label: Net revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago, nominal and constant-dollar

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees based on the payments volume Visa's clients processed in the prior quarter, which rose 8% in constant dollars.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for authorizing, clearing and settling each transaction on Visa's network; processed transactions rose 9%.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used outside its home country — the cross-border business; cross-border volume rose 16% in constant dollars.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services, consulting and other fees.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Salaries and benefits for the people who run the network.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — offices, legal and administration.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and sponsorships that keep the Visa brand in front of cardholders.

opex.name: Litigation provision
opex.note: Setting money aside for legal cases — far below the $341M provided a year ago for the interchange litigation.

opex.name: Network, professional & depreciation
opex.note: Running the network, outside professional help, and wear on Visa's technology — $181M network and processing, $131M professional fees and $247M depreciation and amortization.

otherDetail: Investment income and other income of $275M, partly offset by $187M of interest expense on Visa's debt.

footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $8,634M; this page starts from gross revenue of $11,982M so the $3,348M of client incentives shows as a cost.

takeaways.title: Cross-border stayed hot
takeaways.text: Payments volume rose 8% in constant dollars and processed transactions 9%, while cross-border volume — the most lucrative traffic — jumped 16%, lifting international transaction revenue 8%.

takeaways.title: Every revenue line grew
takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 9% to $8,634M: service revenue +11%, data processing +14%, international transaction +8% and other revenue +18%, against client incentives of $3,348M paid back to card issuers.

takeaways.title: An easy comparison flattered GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Net income rose 17% to $4,890M and EPS 20% to $2.39 — helped by a litigation provision of just $9M versus $341M a year ago. Excluding special items, non-GAAP EPS was $2.41, up 11%. Visa also returned $4.4B to shareholders in buybacks and dividends.

oneTimers: GAAP results include $61M of amortization of acquired intangible assets and acquisition-related costs ($40M of amortization plus $21M of acquisition costs) and $4M of net gains on equity investments. Excluding these items, non-GAAP net income was $4,938M, or $2.41 per share.
